text:
dina: heads up — noticed a recurring pattern where long-sequence tenants (>=200 tokens) keep grabbing most of the token budget and short-seq tenants are getting starved. p99 for short tenants spiked after yesterday's batching tweak.

sam: can you paste the profiler output / queue snapshot? is this correlated with kv-hit behavior?

dina: pasted quick excerpt from the profiler and queue dump: 
```
# perf snapshot 1750012000
tenant_A: avg_seq_len=320, kv_hits=0.62, batch_tokens=768, batches=32
tenant_B: avg_seq_len=16,  kv_hits=0.15, batch_tokens=96,  batches=16
runtime: kernel_swap_count=430, long_kernel_time_p50=120ms, short_kernel_time_p50=30ms
queue_state: long_queue=18, short_queue=3, token_budget_total=2048
```
seems like long tenants are forming big continuous batches and we see kernel switches that favor long-path kernels.

luca: yep — kernel selection + continuous batching interaction is the sneaky part. long sequences get sticky kv-affinity and then the batcher keeps adding to the same slice because token_budget heuristic is naive. result: short tenants wait.

marta: quick ideas: 1) carve out a short_seq reserve (e.g. 15-25% of token budget) 2) short-path fasttrack for seq < 32 3) time-based preemption if short_queue_wait > X ms :clock1:

perf-bot: regression alert (auto): change 1750008500 (batching:window=50ms->70ms) correlated with short-tenant p95 +38ms.

dina: my working hypothesis: high kv_hit for long tenants increases incentive for large batches (cache locality x throughput). batcher refills credits per-slice which favors the active slice. we need fairness in token-crediting, not just request-count balancing.

sam: propose experiments (canary A/B):
- enforce `max_tokens_per_tenant_per_window = 1024`
- add `short_seq_quota = 0.20` (fraction of batch tokens reserved for seq_len <= 32)
- implement preemptive slice steal when short_queue_wait > 50ms (steal up to min(64, slice_tokens/8))

marta: also add telemetry: `per_tenant_batch_token_fraction`, `per_tenant_kernel_switches`, `per_slice_kv_affinity` so we can validate.

luca: small-footprint kernel option: choose a lower-overhead kernel for tiny sequences so the scheduler isn't tempted to combine them into long batches. This reduces the throughput incentive for long-path dominance.

dina: I'll draft a canary config patch and a tiny runtime change that does token-credit smoothing (exponential decay refill) and short_seq fast-path. sample config diff: 
```json
{
  \"batcher\": {
    \"max_tokens_per_tenant_per_window\": 1024,
    \"short_seq_threshold\": 32,
    \"short_seq_quota_fraction\": 0.2,
    \"credit_refill_decay_ms\": 30000
  }
}
```
this is intentionally conservative for canary.

perf-bot: note — add a synthetic load test that mixes 70% short(8-24) + 30% long(200-400) across 20 tenants. record p50/p95/p99 per-tenant.

deploy-bot: scheduling canary deploy to `eng-runtime-canary` at 1750012400 :rocket:

sam: one more: add automatic fallback to a cheaper model/kernel when overall short-tenant wait > threshold. reduces kernel_swap churn.

dina: sounds good. i'll implement the telemetry + canary patch. assigning @sam and @luca to metrics dashboards, @marta to config vet and rollout plan. will report results in ~24h. :thumbsup:
